content.title: Automakers Urge Tariff Relief in Review of North American Trade Pact
content.summary: Car companies urged the Trump administration to secure tariff relief as part of next year's renegotiate of the North American trade pact.  In letters submitted to the United States Trade Representative, automakers said that tariffs on products from Canada and Mexico should be reevaluated when the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement, or USMCA, is reviewed in 2026.  Cars and parts from Mexico and Canada are currently subject to a 25% tariff, with some relief on parts for cars assembled in the U.S.
